senses.definition: A thought expressed in verse; a verse; a poem; a tale told in verse.
(countable) A word that rhymes with another.
examples: Norse poetry is littered with rhymes like “sól … sunnan”.
Rap makes use of rhymes such as “money … honey” and “nope … dope”.

subsenses.definition: (countable, in particular) A word that rhymes with another, in that it is pronounced identically with the other word from the vowel in its stressed syllable to the end.

senses.definition: (uncountable) Rhyming: sameness of letters or sounds of part of some words.
examples: The poem exhibits a peculiar form of rhyme.

senses.definition: (intransitive, followed by with) Of a word, to be pronounced identically with another from the vowel in its stressed syllable to the end.
examples: Creation rhymes with integration and station.
India and windier rhyme with each other in non-rhotic accents.

senses.definition: (reciprocal, of two or more words) To be pronounced identically from the vowel in the stressed syllable of each to the end of each.
(intransitive, of an utterance, text, etc.) To contain words that are pronounced identically to each other from the vowel in the stressed syllable to the end.
examples: I rewrote the story to make it rhyme.

senses.definition: (intransitive, figurative, followed by with) To somewhat resemble or correspond with.
